svg.title: Higher mobility changes drift; more electrons can change current without changing drift
svg.desc: Three different uniform channels have identical geometry, the same prescribed positive field E0, and a matching fixed positive background N_D=n in each. All reference parameters are positive. Define mu_ref=e tau_ref/m_ref, u_ref=mu_ref E0>0 and J_ref=e n_ref u_ref. In the reference channel, n=n_ref, mu=mu_ref, u=-u_ref and J=J_ref. Doubling mobility at fixed density doubles both the leftward electron drift and the rightward current. Doubling density at fixed mobility leaves drift unchanged and doubles current. Arrow lengths are quantitative only when comparing the same quantity across channels, never current against velocity. These are separate low-field models, not time evolution or a claim that doping leaves microscopic scattering fixed.
svg.text: Compare u arrows only with u arrows;
compare J arrows only with J arrows.
